a.raw: its not you they're looking for said the prince
a.fixed: “It’s not you they’re looking for,” said the prince.
a.why: Quotation marks go around the prince’s exact words, and It’s starts them with a capital. It’s needs an apostrophe because it means it is. A comma goes inside the closing quotation mark. A period ends the sentence.

b.raw: well send the whipping boy said billy
b.why: Quotation marks go around Billy’s exact words, and We’ll starts them with a capital. We’ll needs an apostrophe because it means we will. A comma goes inside the closing quotation mark. Billy is a name. A period ends the sentence.

vcloze1.h1: Jemmy cannot understand it. Which bank word means to understand something deep?
vcloze1.why: fathom means to understand something deep.

vcloze2.h1: The outlaws get all mixed up. Which bank word means to confuse someone?
vcloze2.why: flummox means to confuse someone completely.

vcloze3.h1: The two outlaws step outside to talk. Which bank word is a talk between two sides?
vcloze3.why: parley means to talk things over.

vcloze4.h1: Cutwater thinks the prince is fishing for something. Which bank word means that?
vcloze4.why: angling means trying to get something in a clever way.

transcripts.welcome: Welcome back, it’s Opti. No new chapters today. Instead, let’s look back at Chapters 6 through 11. A lot happened in that hut. Think about who held the quill, who gave the orders, and who surprised you. Today you’ll put your whole opinion paragraph together, all five parts.
transcripts.guide1: Review day. You’ll roll the dice for words that share the root that means carry, and you’ll hunt for mistakes in compound sentences. Not every sentence has a mistake, so read each one carefully before you tap. Then fill the last sacks in the wagon.
transcripts.guide2: No new reading today. Flip back through Chapters 6 to 11 and find the moments that stuck with you. Was there a time Jemmy surprised you? A time the prince did? Keep those pages in mind. They’ll help you answer the questions.
transcripts.guide3: This is the big one. Today you put all five parts together: your claim, your reason, your example, the other side, and your conclusion. Read Clara’s paragraph first, and notice how each part leads to the next. Then build yours, one sentence at a time.

notes.wordParts: The root port means “carry.” transport = carry across, import = carry in, export = carry out, report = carry back, portable = able to be carried.
notes.grammar: A compound sentence joins two complete thoughts with a comma and a joining word: Jemmy wrote the note, and Billy watched.
notes.spelling: When a word ends in a consonant + le, that consonant goes with the le to make the last syllable: ta·ble, can·dle, sim·ple.
notes.wgrd: Good readers look back at the whole section and ask how each character has changed since the start.
vocab: to understand something very deep or hard
a talk between two sides who disagree
trying in a clever way to get something

mods.todo: Listen to Opti. Then tap the lens you will use today.
mods.script: [warmly] There are no new chapters today. Instead, good readers look back at everything they've read so far. Think about Jemmy and the prince in Chapter 1, back at the castle. Now think about them in the outlaws' hut. How has each boy changed? Then tap one of the two lenses below to use while you look back. You don't need to write anything.

mods.todo: Tap the yellow parts. Then pick Sentence A or B and type it the right way.
mods.script: Let's fix a sentence. Look at the correct one first. The prince is talking, so his words go inside quotation marks. Doesn't has an apostrophe, because it's short for does not. And a comma goes before the closing quotation mark, because the sentence keeps going: Prince Brat said coldly. Tap the yellow parts to see each rule. Then pick Sentence A or Sentence B, and type it the right way. Watch out, the sentence you fix needs two apostrophes!

mods.todo: Make up a haiku about something outside your window. Count 5, 7, 5. Say it out loud.
mods.script: Here are the two cold-morning haiku again. Today, you'll make up your own. Look out your window. What do you see? A bird, a car, the rain, a tree? Make up three lines about it, and count the beats on your fingers. Five, then seven, then five. Try to save a little surprise for the last line. Say your haiku out loud. You don't need to write it.

mods.todo: Tap Roll the Dice. Say what the word means. Tap Check My Thinking. Roll all six words.
mods.script: Roll it, then crack it. Every word on the dice has port in it, so you already know half the meaning. Look at the part in front of port. That part is your clue. Say what the whole word means out loud, then tap Check My Thinking. Do all six.

mods.todo: Fill in each sentence with a word from the word bank. Tap Check My Work. Then play the matching game.
mods.script: Last chance with this week's words: fathom, flummox, parley, and angling. Here's a trick. Read each sentence out loud with the word in the blank. If it sounds right and makes sense, keep it. Then tap Check My Work.

mods.todo: Tap the word where the mistake is, or tap No mistake. Then tap See the answers and answer the question in the box.
mods.script: Can you spot what's wrong? The fog was thick but, they kept going. The comma jumped to the wrong side of but! It belongs right before it. Read each sentence. Tap the word where the mistake is, or tap No mistake if it's right.

Look back at the whole week. Jemmy wrote the ransom note, played the prince, and tricked two outlaws. Was he helping the prince, or helping himself? Maybe both! Now think about the prince. He could have gone home, and he said no. What do you think he really wants?

mods.todo: Read the two questions. Then look back through Ch. 6–11 in your book.
mods.script: There are no new chapters today. Instead, look back through Chapters 6 to 11 in your book. First, read the two Pause and Think questions below. One is about something Jemmy says to the prince: It's not me you think you're protecting, is it? The other asks if the prince has really changed. Flip back through the pages to find clues. Then do the Read Like a Writer box.

mods.todo: Pick Explorer or Scholar. Answer the three questions in full sentences.
mods.script: Now look back and answer in full sentences, with details from the book. One, Jemmy signs the note as the prince. How does that help him, and how could it hurt him? Two, describe one moment in Chapter 11 when the prince does something unexpected. Three, who is cleverer in Chapters 6 to 11, Jemmy or the prince? Give one example for each boy. For a challenge, pick Scholar, and add one more detail to each answer.

mods.todo: Write your paragraph with all five parts: claim, reason, example, the other side, and conclusion.
mods.script: Today you put it all together. Clara had five pieces: her claim, a reason, an example, the other side, and a conclusion. Then she put them in order to make one paragraph. Read hers and listen to how it flows. It starts with her claim, gives a reason, proves it with an example from Chapter 2, answers the other side, and ends with a conclusion. Now write your own paragraph in the box, with all five parts. Use your work from this week to help.

virtue.name: courage
virtue.title: Courage Watch: Did they show courage?

items.t: Jemmy writes the ransom note and signs it with the prince’s name.
items.why: He takes a big risk to trick the outlaws.

items.t: The prince gobbles an apple tart and says he will go back “when I choose.”
items.why: Doing what he wants is not the same as courage.

items.t: Billy pulls off his belt. Jemmy speaks up with the horse idea.
items.why: He is scared, but he speaks up to stop it.
